title: Wave operators and the nonlinear scattering map
notes: The notes write \(U(t)U(s)=U(t+s)\), conservation of \(E\), and \(E(U(t)f-U_0(t)f_\pm)\to0\) as \(t\to\pm\infty\). The relation between \(f_-\) and \(f_+\) is denoted \(S\).
statement: Let \(U(t)\) and \(U_0(t)\) be global flows on specified phase spaces embedded in a common normed space \(X\). A scattering state for \(f\) is an \(f_\pm\) with \(\|U(t)f-U_0(t)f_\pm\|_X\to0\). If these states exist uniquely on specified incoming and outgoing sets, the scattering map is \(S:f_-\mapsto f_+\). Existence, uniqueness, and surjectivity are separate assertions; conservation of an energy alone implies none of them.
reconstruction: The normed phase space, domains of the maps, and uniqueness assumptions make the definition precise. Interpreting the notebook's \(E\) on a difference as a norm or a coercive error functional is a reconstruction.
fate: This is exposition of an existing framework. Strauss's 1973 Denver lectures were published in 1974; the abstract and opening formulation of \citet[pp.~53--78]{strauss1974scattering} explicitly study asymptotic comparison with linear equations. The publication is not a theorem verifying all examples listed here.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The framework is standard; no universal existence or completeness assertion can be extracted from this paragraph.

title: The cubic Klein--Gordon equation as a scattering example
notes: The displayed example is \(u_{tt}-\Delta u+u+|u|^2u=0\), called a wave equation. The Laplacian sign is retraced in the manuscript.
statement: For a sufficiently regular real or complex solution on \(\mathbb R^d\), with decay justifying integration by parts, the defocusing cubic Klein--Gordon energy is \[E(u,u_t)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\left(\tfrac12|u_t|^2+\tfrac12|\nabla u|^2+\tfrac12|u|^2+\tfrac14|u|^4\right)\,dx.\] It is conserved. A scattering theorem additionally fixes \(d\), a solution class, and a norm; the notebook does not supply them.
reconstruction: The energy and the identification as Klein--Gordon are our standard reconstruction of the displayed equation, not a recorded theorem of global scattering.
fate: The example belongs to the nonlinear-wave scattering program advertised in \citet[abstract and pp.~53--78]{strauss1974scattering}. Only the program and bibliographic chronology were verified there; the notebook does not identify a particular theorem with fixed dimension and data.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The equation and its conserved energy are identifiable. A claim of all-data scattering in an arbitrary dimension would go beyond the evidence.

title: KdV and the distinction between dispersive and soliton asymptotics
notes: The second example is \(u_\tau+u_{xxx}+uu_x=0\), labelled the de Vries equation.
statement: This is the Korteweg--de Vries equation after a normalization of the dependent variable. Its nonzero travelling solitons show why the preceding comparison with the free Airy flow cannot be asserted for every decaying solution without specifying the asymptotic sector. The equation itself is unambiguous; no scattering theorem is stated.
reconstruction: The warning about solitons interprets the example; it is not attributed to Gelfand. The manuscript's \(\tau\) is retained as a time variable.
fate: \citet[pp.~240--243]{zabuskykruskal1965solitons} had already connected KdV solitary-wave interactions with recurrence in 1965. The publisher record confirms the paper and date; this supports chronology, not an exact identification of the unspecified scattering statement.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: An expository example of nonlinear dispersive asymptotics, with no precise new problem in the notes.

title: Cartier's 2-adic logarithm example
notes: ``\ru{(Cartier) в изложении Гельфанда}'' precedes \(\ln(1-a)=a+a^2/2+\cdots\), followed by \(a=2\), \(\ln(-1)=0\), and \(\sum_{n\ge1}2^n/n=0\). The partial sums begin \(2,4,20/3,32/3\).
statement: In \(\mathbb Q_2\), \(v_2(2^n/n)=n-v_2(n)\to\infty\), so the series converges. The logarithm on \(1+2\mathbb Z_2\) is \(\log(1-a)=-\sum_{n\ge1}a^n/n\). Its homomorphism law gives \(2\log(-1)=\log(1)=0\), hence \(\sum_{n\ge1}2^n/n=0\). Thus for every \(k\), all sufficiently late partial sums belong to \(2^k\mathbb Z_2\).
reconstruction: We insert the missing minus sign and justify convergence; the final vanishing assertion survives this correction. The source gives an oral attribution, not a Cartier publication.
fate: An elementary consequence of the pre-existing \(p\)-adic logarithm. No exact Cartier publication was located; the mathematical verification here is direct and does not turn an oral attribution into a bibliography entry.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Correct after repairing the logarithm identity; the attribution remains an oral report in the notebook.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand (after Cartier)

title: The metaplectic obstruction and symplectic spinors
notes: For symplectic \(M\), the frame group is \(\operatorname{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)\), topologically \(U(n)\); a two-sheeted cover \(M(2n,\mathbb R)\) permits a spinor bundle when \(C_1\) is divisible by two.
statement: Let \((M^{2n},\omega)\) be a smooth symplectic manifold and \(J\) an \(\omega\)-compatible almost complex structure. Its symplectic frame bundle lifts to \(\operatorname{Mp}(2n,\mathbb R)\) exactly when \(w_2(TM)=0\), equivalently \(c_1(TM,J)\in2H^2(M;\mathbb Z)\). A chosen lift and the oscillator representation define an associated infinite-dimensional symplectic spinor bundle. The homotopy equivalence with \(U(n)\) is not an isomorphism of groups.
reconstruction: The standard name \(\operatorname{Mp}\), the choice of compatible \(J\), and the equivalence with \(w_2=0\) explicate the shorthand. A choice of lift is necessary, not canonical.
fate: The notes explicitly report Kostant's work. \citet[\S3, Theorem~5 and Definition~6]{krysl2017spinors} states this obstruction and associated-bundle construction, attributing it to Kostant's 1973 Rome contribution published in 1974. The underlying metaplectic representation predates the seminar; publication in 1974 does not make this Kirillov's new result.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: An established construction, with the topological obstruction and choice of metaplectic structure made explicit.

title: Canonical commutation relations and metaplectic implementation
notes: The algebra has \(p_iq_j-q_jp_i=\delta_{ij}\), represented by \(p_i=\partial_{x_i}\), \(q_i=x_i\) in \(L^2(\mathbb R^n)\). Symplectic changes of generators are said to induce automorphisms of bounded operators, implemented up to scalar, whose factors reduce to \(\pm1\).
statement: On the invariant Schwartz domain, \([\partial_{x_i},x_j]=\delta_{ij}\), together with \([p_i,p_j]=[q_i,q_j]=0\). For a unitary formulation use \(P_i=-i\partial_{x_i}\), \(Q_i=x_i\) and the Weyl relations of the Heisenberg group with a fixed nontrivial central character. Uniqueness of its irreducible unitary representation gives projective implementers for \(\operatorname{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)\); their canonical lift is the oscillator representation of its double cover.
reconstruction: The domain and the Weyl form of the relations repair the unsupported passage from unbounded polynomial generators to bounded-operator automorphisms. The double cover requires the metaplectic construction; innerness alone does not prove it.
fate: \citet[\S\S2.1--2.3]{krysl2017spinors} reviews the precise oscillator representation and Weyl algebra. Kostant's earlier quantization paper was published in 1970, independently of the website's later digitization date \citep[pp.~87--208]{kostant1970quantization}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The representation-theoretic statement is established. The notebook proof needs domain and continuity hypotheses and a genuine metaplectic step.

title: The Clifford-algebra analogy
notes: The parenthesis says that replacing the minus sign by a plus gives the spin representation of the orthogonal group.
statement: For a finite-dimensional quadratic space \((V,q)\) over a field of characteristic different from two, the Clifford algebra is generated by \(V\) with \(uv+vu=2b(u,v)\), where \(b\) polarizes \(q\). Its spin modules carry representations of \(\operatorname{Spin}(V,q)\), hence generally projective representations of \(\operatorname{SO}(V,q)\). Merely changing the displayed mixed commutator is insufficient: all anticommutation relations and the quadratic form must be specified.
reconstruction: This is an analogy reconstructed as a Clifford-algebra statement; the notebook contains no choice of signature or spin module.
fate: The orthogonal/symplectic analogy is reviewed in \citet[\S2 and introduction]{krysl2017spinors}. It is background, not an independent 1973 discovery.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Standard after specifying the full Clifford relations and the spin double cover.

title: Bounded K-valued measures as continuous duals
notes: For a finite extension \(K/\mathbb Q_p\), the notes write \(\operatorname{Hom}(C(\mathbb Z_p,K),\mathbb Q_p)=C(\mathbb Z_p,K)'=M(\mathbb Z_p,K)\).
statement: Give \(C(\mathbb Z_p,K)\) its supremum norm. The Banach space of bounded \(K\)-valued measures is \(M(\mathbb Z_p,K)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K,\mathrm{cont}}(C(\mathbb Z_p,K),K)\), with operator norm. Equivalently these are finitely additive \(K\)-valued functions on compact open sets with uniformly bounded values, extended to continuous functions by uniform approximation.
reconstruction: We specify continuity and \(K\)-linearity and change the codomain to \(K\). A \(\mathbb Q_p\)-linear dual is a different object, though trace pairings can relate it to a \(K\)-dual after extra choices.
fate: \citet[\S2]{amice1965mesures} explicitly defines the measure space as the continuous dual; the lecture is dated 17 May 1965. The note's codomain mismatch is not part of that result.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established Banach-space duality; the coefficient field and boundedness cannot be suppressed.

title: Convolution of p-adic measures
notes: Convolution is defined by the iterated integral \(\int f\,d(\mu*\nu)=\int\int f(x+y)\,d\mu(x)\,d\nu(y)\).
statement: For bounded \(K\)-valued measures on the compact additive group \(\mathbb Z_p\), this formula defines a bounded measure. Uniform continuity makes the inner integral continuous in \(y\). It gives a commutative unital Banach algebra with unit \(\delta_0\) and \(\|\mu*\nu\|\le\|\mu\|\|\nu\|\).
reconstruction: The compact group, boundedness, and unit are stated explicitly to justify the integral construction.
fate: The same construction appears in \citet[\S2, ``Produit de convolution'']{amice1965mesures}, eight years before this seminar.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: An established convolution algebra; no unbounded-measure extension follows automatically.

title: The bounded Amice transform
notes: ``Theorem 1'' identifies \(M(\mathbb Z_p,K)\) with \(K[[T]]\), immediately restricted to series of finite coefficient supremum. It uses \(a_k=\int\binom{x}{k}\,d\mu\) and \(\int(1+T)^x\,d\mu\).
statement: Write \[K[[T]]_{\mathrm b}=\{\sum a_kT^k:\sup_k|a_k|_p<\infty\}.\] The map \(\mathcal A\mu(T)=\sum_{k\ge0}(\int\binom{x}{k}\,d\mu)T^k\) is an isometric \(K\)-algebra isomorphism \(M(\mathbb Z_p,K)\simeq K[[T]]_{\mathrm b}\). In particular \(\mathcal A(\mu*\nu)=\mathcal A\mu\,\mathcal A\nu\). The integral character formula converges for \(|T|_p<1\).
reconstruction: The subscript distinguishes the bounded-coefficient algebra from all formal series; the notebook's finite-norm parenthesis already supplies that restriction.
fate: \citet[\S3]{amice1965mesures} identifies convolution measures with bounded-coefficient analytic transforms and records the isometry. The one-variable identification in the notes is its standard special case.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established; the equality with unrestricted formal power series would be false.

title: Unbounded distributions are not automatically arbitrary moment series
notes: The notes say that formal series are obtained from unbounded measures, then define such measures as finitely additive functions on elementary sets, dual to locally constant functions.
statement: The algebraic dual of locally constant functions on \(\mathbb Z_p\) consists of compatible values on residue classes, without a uniform bound. It does not by that definition act on the non-locally-constant polynomials \(\binom{x}{k}\). Thus the displayed moment transform is not defined for an arbitrary such distribution. A distribution space with additional regularity and a growth-controlled transform must be specified before any power-series classification is meaningful.
reconstruction: This is a diagnosis of the missing domain, not a replacement theorem asserting a particular distribution topology.
fate: The bounded theorem in \citet[\S\S2--3]{amice1965mesures} does not establish this unbounded extension. Searches for Amice's duals and Fourier transforms identify several inequivalent distribution theories; none supplies the absent test-function space in this sentence.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The literal inference is unsupported. Its intended unbounded version cannot be identified from the notes; this is not evidence for an open problem.

title: Measures on the p-adic unit group
notes: ``Theorem 2'' writes \(M(\mathbb Z_p^*,K)=(p-1)K[[T]]\).
statement: For odd \(p\), \(\mathbb Z_p^\times\simeq\mu_{p-1}\times(1+p\mathbb Z_p)\), and a choice of a topological generator identifies the second factor with \(\mathbb Z_p\). Since \(K\supset\mathbb Q_p\) contains \(\mu_{p-1}\), character idempotents give \(M(\mathbb Z_p^\times,K)\simeq\prod_{\chi:\mu_{p-1}\to K^\times}K[[T]]_{\mathrm b}\). For \(p=2\), use \(\{\pm1\}\times(1+4\mathbb Z_2)\), giving two components, not \(p-1=1\).
reconstruction: We interpret the coefficient \(p-1\) as a product decomposition of convolution algebras, add the odd-prime restriction, and make the noncanonical generator choice explicit.
fate: This is a direct finite-character decomposition combined with the already established one-variable transform of \citet[\S3]{amice1965mesures}; the decomposition is reconstructed here, not quoted as that paper's numbered theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Correct for odd primes in the stated form; the dyadic case requires a different finite factor.

title: Exponential coordinates and the range of the transform
notes: Putting \(1+T=e^\tau\), the notes write \(\widetilde\mu(\tau)=\int e^{\tau x}\,d\mu\), invite one to ``rewrite the analysis'', and ask what functions arise, with integral coefficients after inverse substitution.
statement: For the already defined bounded measures, \(\widetilde\mu(\tau)=\mathcal A\mu(e^\tau-1)\) converges for \(|\tau|_p<p^{-1/(p-1)}\). Formally, \(G(\tau)\in K[[\tau]]\) is in this image exactly when \(G(\log(1+T))\in K[[T]]_{\mathrm b}\); the integral-measure unit ball corresponds to coefficients in \(\mathcal O_K\). Analytic continuation outside this exponential disk is a separate question and is not specified in the notes.
reconstruction: This exact formal characterization is our consequence of the preceding isomorphism. We do not replace the informal request for a range description by an unrecorded continuation problem.
fate: The character transform is already developed in \citet[\S3]{amice1965mesures}; the exponential-coordinate formulation here follows by a change of formal variable. No distinct publication or unresolved analytic-domain question is identifiable from the notebook wording.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The bounded formal range is determined by the transform theorem. A broader analytic range question lacks a specified domain and topology.

title: The Newton--Mahler expansion and norm identity
notes: The proof uses \(P_k(x)=x(x-1)\cdots(x-k+1)/k!\), \(c_k=\Delta^kf(0)\), and claims uniform convergence for every continuous \(f\), with \(\max|f|=\max|a_k|\). The series is called Taylor and then Maclaurin.
statement: Every \(f\in C(\mathbb Z_p,K)\) has the unique uniformly convergent expansion \(f(x)=\sum_{k\ge0}c_k\binom{x}{k}\), where \(c_k=\sum_{j=0}^k(-1)^{k-j}\binom{k}{j}f(j)\to0\), and \(\|f\|_\infty=\sup_k|c_k|\). Duality gives \(\|\mu\|=\sup_k|\int\binom{x}{k}\,d\mu|\). These are finite differences and falling factorials, not derivatives and ordinary powers.
reconstruction: The vanishing of the coefficients and uniqueness are supplied. The \(a_k\) in the last norm formula refers to function-expansion coefficients there; elsewhere it denotes measure moments.
fate: This is Mahler's 1958 interpolation theorem \citep[Theorem~1]{mahler1958interpolation}, extended in \citet[Chapter~II]{amice1964interpolation}. Mahler's 1961 correction concerns the differentiability theorem, not this continuous expansion \citep[opening paragraph]{mahler1961correction}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established; the notebook name ``Maclaurin must not be read as a claim of ordinary analyticity for every continuous p-adic function.

title: Quillen's Q-category of an exact category
notes: \(M\) is an additive full subcategory of an abelian category, closed under extensions. Objects of \(QM\) are those of \(M\); a morphism is drawn \(X\leftarrow X''\to X'\), with an admissible epimorphism and an admissible monomorphism.
statement: Let \(\mathcal M\) be an essentially small extension-closed additive full subcategory of an abelian category, with the induced exact structure. A morphism \(X\to Y\) in \(Q\mathcal M\) is an isomorphism class of spans \(X\xleftarrow{p}Z\xrightarrow{i}Y\), with \(p\) an admissible epimorphism and \(i\) an admissible monomorphism. Composition uses pullback; the exact-category axioms ensure admissibility.
reconstruction: We insert smallness, the induced exact structure, equivalence of spans, and the composition law. These are necessary to turn the diagram into a category.
fate: \citet[\S2, construction of \(Q\mathcal M\)]{quillen1973higher} is the exact source, originating in the 1972 Seattle lectures and published in 1973. This continues the exposition in record 311.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established; there is no separate Fuchs conjecture here.

title: The missing loop in comparison with the plus construction
notes: The notebook states that \(BQM\) is homologically equivalent to \(B\operatorname{GL}(\infty,A)\).
statement: For a unital ring \(A\), let \(\mathcal P(A)\) be its exact category of finitely generated projective modules. Then \(\Omega BQ\mathcal P(A)\simeq K_0(A)\times B\operatorname{GL}(A)^+\), after choosing compatible base components. Thus the component of the constant loop has the homotopy type of \(B\operatorname{GL}(A)^+\), and the plus map from \(B\operatorname{GL}(A)\) is an integral homology equivalence. The statement does not concern \(BQ\mathcal P(A)\) itself.
reconstruction: The ring, category, loop-space shift, and component are supplied. For example \(H_1(BQ\mathcal P(\mathbb F_2))\cong K_0(\mathbb F_2)=\mathbb Z\), whereas \(H_1(B\operatorname{GL}(\mathbb F_2))=0\), so the literal line cannot be retained.
fate: The comparison is announced in \citet[introduction, pp.~86--87]{quillen1973higher}, which expressly defers its proof; see the later treatment in \citet[Chapter~IV, Q-construction]{weibel2013kbook}. The corrected theorem was already available in the 1972--1973 work.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established with the loop and component restored. The displayed notebook comparison is false as written.

title: K-zero as the fundamental group of BQ
notes: The Grothendieck group is generated by objects with relations \(X=X'+X''\) from short exact sequences; the notes identify it with \(K_0(M)=\pi_1(BQM,0)\).
statement: For an essentially small exact category \(\mathcal M\), let \(K_0(\mathcal M)\) be the abelian group on isomorphism classes \([X]\), modulo \([X]=[X']+[X'']\) for every admissible short exact sequence. There is a canonical isomorphism \(K_0(\mathcal M)\cong\pi_1(BQ\mathcal M,0)\).
reconstruction: Isomorphism classes and admissibility are explicit. The split exact sequences explain commutativity but do not replace the nonsplit relations.
fate: This is the basic \(K_0\)-identification in \citet[\S2]{quillen1973higher}, circulated in the 1972 Seattle lectures and published in 1973.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: A standard theorem; the indexing of homotopy groups is correct in this line.

title: Object loops and additivity through two-simplices
notes: For each \(X\), the sketch defines a loop \(\zeta_X\) through \(0\) and \(X\). The triangular picture for \(0\to X'\to X\to X''\to0\) yields \(\zeta_X\sim\zeta_{X'}\zeta_{X''}\), invoking two-simplices.
statement: There are two canonical \(Q\)-arrows \(0\to X\): the spans \(0\leftarrow0\to X\) and \(0\leftarrow X\xrightarrow{1}X\). Traversing the first and then the reverse of the second gives a based loop, with a choice of global sign convention. The nerve's two-simplices associated with an admissible exact sequence identify its class with the product of the corresponding classes for \(X'\) and \(X''\).
reconstruction: The backwards path is a path in the realization, not an inverse morphism in \(Q\mathcal M\). We spell out the spans to disambiguate the diagram.
fate: This is the elementary nerve proof underlying \citet[\S2, calculation of \(\pi_1\)]{quillen1973higher}, not a new additivity theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: An identifiable proof of the preceding theorem; the diagram is meaningful after distinguishing arrows from reversed paths.

title: Darboux coordinates and symplectic transition functions
notes: Locally \(\omega=\sum dp_k\wedge dq_k\), and tangent-bundle transition maps lie in \(\operatorname{Sp}(2n,\mathbb R)\). They are assumed lifted to the two-sheeted cover.
statement: Every smooth symplectic \(2n\)-manifold has Darboux charts in which \(\omega\) has the displayed form. Derivatives of coordinate changes preserve \(\omega\) and therefore are symplectic linear maps pointwise. A metaplectic structure is a compatible cocycle of lifts, not merely separate lifts of individual transition functions.
reconstruction: We distinguish nonlinear coordinate changes from their derivatives, and impose the cocycle condition on the lifts.
fate: This is the local and bundle background used in \citet[\S3]{krysl2017spinors}; the topological obstruction is item 1973-312.1. No new local normal-form theorem is proposed.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Standard Darboux and principal-bundle theory.

title: The Schwartz--Hilbert--distribution triple of spinor bundles
notes: The spinor representation induces \(HM\), with \(SM\subset HM\subset S'M\); \(SM\) is labelled rapidly decreasing.
statement: Given a metaplectic principal bundle \(P\to M\), the invariant triple \(\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)\subset L^2(\mathbb R^n)\subset\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^n)\) yields associated bundles \(P\times_{\operatorname{Mp}}\mathcal S\), \(P\times_{\operatorname{Mp}}L^2\), and \(P\times_{\operatorname{Mp}}\mathcal S'\). The Hilbert embedding in tempered distributions uses the usual pairing convention. These are infinite-dimensional bundles with their respective locally convex topologies.
reconstruction: The fibre models, topology, and chosen metaplectic structure are supplied; \(S'M\) is a distribution bundle, not the algebraic dual of all sections.
fate: The spinor bundle and oscillator realization are described in \citet[\S\S2.2--3.1]{krysl2017spinors}; \citet[\S3, Definition~2]{krysl2006spinor} also constructs the associated bundle. This records Kostant's existing construction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: An established construction. The representation preserves Schwartz space, so the three fibres glue compatibly.

title: The Heisenberg bundle and the polynomial degree error
notes: \(GM=TM\oplus(\mathbb R\times M)\) is called the Heisenberg Lie algebra bundle and is labelled polynomials of degree at most two in \(p,q\). It acts on the spinor bundle.
statement: The fibre \(T_xM\oplus\mathbb R\) with \([(v,a),(w,b)]=(0,\omega_x(v,w))\) is the \((2n+1)\)-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra. Under Poisson brackets it corresponds to affine-linear polynomials, of degree at most one. Polynomials of degree at most two form the larger semidirect extension by \(\mathfrak{sp}(2n,\mathbb R)\). Its infinitesimal Schrödinger action is defined on the Schwartz fibres, not as bounded operators on every Hilbert fibre.
reconstruction: We repair the degree and specify the invariant domain of the action. The central normalization may be rescaled consistently.
fate: The Heisenberg and Weyl-algebra realization is standard background in \citet[\S\S2.1--2.3]{krysl2017spinors}. A dimension count already separates the two polynomial algebras.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The named Heisenberg construction is established; the degree-two label is a faithful notebook error.

title: Lagrangian tangent planes
notes: The final line introduces \(RM\) and \(R_x\), Lagrangian subspaces of \(T_xM\) of maximal dimension.
statement: A subspace \(L\subset T_xM\) is Lagrangian if \(\omega_x|_L=0\) and \(\dim L=n\), equivalently \(L=L^{\perp_\omega}\). All such planes form the fibre of the Lagrangian Grassmannian bundle over \(M\). A global section is additional structure and is not asserted to exist.
reconstruction: The equality of maximal isotropic dimension with half the tangent dimension is made explicit. The notation does not identify a chosen polarization.
fate: This is standard symplectic linear algebra in the setting reviewed by \citet[\S3]{krysl2017spinors}; Fuchs's short intervention on P000529 continues the bundle description.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: An established definition, with no existence theorem for a Lagrangian distribution in the notes.

title: The nonlinear chain equation and its Hamiltonian sign
notes: The displayed chain has \(\ddot x_k=x_{k-1}+x_{k+1}-2x_k+\varepsilon(x_{k-1}-x_k)^2+\varepsilon(x_{k+1}-x_k)^2\). Both nonlinear signs are positive in the scan.
statement: For a nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian chain with \(r_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), potential \(V(r)=r^2/2+\varepsilon r^3/3\), and compatible fixed or periodic boundary conditions, \(\ddot x_k=V'(r_k)-V'(r_{k-1})\). Hence the quadratic terms occur as \(\varepsilon[(x_{k+1}-x_k)^2-(x_k-x_{k-1})^2]\). The notebook equation is a different dynamical system unless an omitted convention changes the model.
reconstruction: The Hamiltonian and boundary-condition alternatives specify the standard alpha-FPU reconstruction. We do not silently edit the source or claim that its plus-plus equation has the same conservation law.
fate: The FPU numerical experiment was reported in \citet[LA-1940]{fermipastaulam1955studies}, written in May 1955. The primary report record was checked; the Hamiltonian differentiation above supplies the sign check independently.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The standard FPU model is identifiable, but its equation is not faithfully represented by the two nonlinear plus signs.

title: Numerical recurrence of low-mode energy
notes: For a chain labelled 16, the initial displacement is sinusoidal, with all energy in the first harmonic. The sketch shows transfer to other modes and near return. A cubic nonlinearity is said to give the same qualitative result.
statement: The identifiable claim is an observation for particular finite nonlinear chains and initial conditions: modal energies may show pronounced near recurrence rather than rapid equipartition. It is not exact periodicity, not a statement for every initial condition, and not a bound uniform in chain length or energy.
reconstruction: We distinguish a numerical observation from a quantified theorem. The notebook does not specify amplitudes, coupling strength, endpoint convention, or the formula used to define modal energy.
fate: The phenomenon is the already reported FPU experiment \citep[LA-1940]{fermipastaulam1955studies}; the connection with soliton recurrence was studied by \citet[pp.~240--243]{zabuskykruskal1965solitons}. Both precede the talk.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The historical phenomenon is established, but the particular plotted experiment is not reproducible from these notes alone.

title: Unidentified recurrence times and integration-step comments
notes: The notes contain \(t=10^{-35}\), a caption approximately 50 million periods, and comments about ten steps and a one-third period. No physical units or numerical algorithm are given.
statement: No definite numerical estimate can be reconstructed: it is not stated which time scale, error tolerance, integration scheme, or physical system the numbers refer to. The figure supports only the qualitative recurrence item 1973-316.2.
reconstruction: We retain the negative exponent seen in the scan rather than changing it to match a plausible timescale. The disconnected numbers are not used as data for a computation.
fate: Comparison with the identifiable FPU report \citep[LA-1940]{fermipastaulam1955studies} does not determine these units or the stated step counts. No exact numerical publication match was found.
